From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>

Cc: Sarah Lin <sarah@pulsar.ai>, Procurement <procurement@acme-corp.com>

Subject: QBR readying — decision grid and scope nominations

Team — kicking off a short thread to crystallize what we need for the QBR packet and the decision grid I promised execs. Main asks below; please read and react inline by EOD local time so I can fold into the deck.

Key context (30k): Acme is evaluating expansion into Dedicated; they want predictable latency and cost targets. We have an ask list from their Procurement (cc'd) and an outline from Sarah on priority use cases.

Immediate asks (can be one-liners):
- Vanessa: confirm which 2 infra blockers (billing SLA and k8s tenant isolation) we can commit to for a Nov pilot.
- Markus: provide a terse cost/latency delta table for the three model variants (open-7B, redwood-architected-13B, redwood-quant-13B) — one slide worth.
- All: mark any items that require an exec sign-off (credits, third-party integrations, SLA exceptions).

Attachments: QBR-deck-v2.pdf (draft slides), decision-grid-v1.xlsx (template).

I will synthesize answers into a single decision grid by 2pm PT and share back for a quick sign-off.

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: QBR readying — decision grid and scope nominations

Vivek — quick answers inline.

- Infra blockers for Nov pilot: billing SLA (we can offer a time-limited credit-backed SLA with legal sign-off) — YES; k8s tenant isolation: partial — we can provide network isolation + node pools but full tenant-level RBAC changes will need infra team's 2-week window.
- Exec sign-offs needed: SLA credits -> yes (Finance/CEO), any KMS/HSM onboarding for Acme -> Security + Legal.

Notes: I'll attach a 1-pager with the infra mitigation plan by noon. If we scope the pilot to a single region (us-west-2) we can shave ~20% off the initial infra lead time.

Vanessa
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Lin <sarah@pulsar.ai>, Procurement <procurement@acme-corp.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 12:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: QBR readying — decision grid and scope nominations

Adding the delta table (summary below) — full numbers in decision-grid-v1.xlsx. Short summary for slide:

- open-7B: lowest infra cost, higher latency tail at p99 for long contexts, recommended for low-cost embedding or batched workloads.
- redwood-architected-13B: better quality, ~1.6x token cost vs open-7B, steady latency; good baseline for mixed workloads.
- redwood-quant-13B: 0.9x token cost of architected-13B, slight quality drop on long-form; best fit for latency-sensitive production endpoints.

Recommendation for Acme pilot: run architected-13B for customer-facing features and quant-13B for internal analytics endpoints; include fallback policy to open-7B under heavy load.

Markus
Director, Serving Runtime
